newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Somali militiamen seize Kenya ship, demand $15,000.
newsitem.headline: Somali militiamen seize Kenya ship, demand $15,000.

text.p: Somali gunmen seized a Kenyan cargo ship off the southern port of Kismayo and are demanding $15,000 for its release, Somali port officials said on Monday.
They told Reuters by radio from Kismayo that eight militiamen using speedboats on Saturday seized the Clove carrying consumer goods from Mombasa, Kenya, before it could enter the port to unload.

Mohamed Abdulle, Kismayo port manager, said the militiamen wanted $15,000 and had contacted the owner of the ship in Mombasa. He said the ship remained on Monday near the port but had no more details.
Nairobi's East African Standard newspaper said on Monday the ship had 20 crew and the militiamen were demanding $100 million.
It said the militiamen posed as coastguards when they approached the ship in speedboats near the port of Mogadishu.
Somalia has had no government since the overthrow of late dictator Mohamed Siad Barre in 1991.
The Regional Piracy Centre of the International Maritime Bureau in Kuala Lumpur said on Monday pirate attacks on ships rose by five to a record 175 incidents worldwide last year.

It said incidents of ships being boarded increased to 124 in 1996 from 110 in 1995. Hijackings declined to five cases from 11 and the number of cases where vessels were fired upon fell to six from nine.
